scope: Segment 132 field-level rules, applicability within the CA Public Key File Load Request, and serialization

rules.title: Segment 132 belongs to the CA Public Key File Load Request's Data Section 3, alongside optional companions 101, 102, 104, 111
rules.note: PROVISIONAL: the exact R/O/C designation for Segment 132 within the CA Public Key File Load Request's own Data Section 3 table was not captured with full certainty during extraction (the segment name strongly implies Required, mirroring Segment 100/108/130's 'anchor segment' pattern, but this should be confirmed rather than assumed). Pending SME confirmation (SEG132-SME-001).

rules.title: Segment Type is fixed value 132, sourced at the Device
Segment Length is 3 digits (not 4 — Segment 132 is NOT one of the seven 4-digit-length segments)
Segment 132 maximum length is 77 alphanumeric characters (01-77/a-z/A-Z)
rules.note: PROVISIONAL: the sum of documented fixed-field lengths (3+3+6+13+1+4+8+8+25+3 = 74) does not exactly reconcile to 77; the difference (3) may reflect separator-counting conventions not fully specified for this segment. Pending SME confirmation (SEG132-SME-002).

rules.title: Sequence Number (Element 86) is required, 6 digits; a limited range (100000-199999) applies ONLY when using the Multithreaded Dial Protocol Communications header for a CAPK File Load
Terminal Identifier (Element 102) is required, 13 characters; for EMV, the first two characters (Device Type) must be '+*' regardless of the actual device type
Load Type (Element 48) is required, fixed value 'K' (indicates Public Key information is requested)
Hardware Version (Element 43), Software Version (Element 96), and Firmware Version (Element 39) are all required device-version identifiers
CA Public Key File Checksum (Element 187) is required in Segment 132, identifying the checksum currently in use — a THIRD segment (after 130 request, 131 response) referencing this same element

Block Number (Element 11) is required, 3 digits, identifying the specific data block requested by a device or sent by the host — implying a multi-block CA key file transfer protocol not fully detailed in this section
rules.note: PROVISIONAL: the block-by-block transfer mechanism (how multiple blocks of the CA key file are requested/delivered) is not detailed in Section 12.22 itself. Pending SME confirmation (SEG132-SME-003) on whether this is in scope for this training pass.

rules.title: Field Separator placement is only explicitly shown for fields 1-2 and 2-3 in the extracted table (via inline <FS> markers); no summary sentence documents separator behavior for fields 4-10
rules.note: PROVISIONAL: unlike most other segments, Section 12.22 lacks the usual 'Note: Field Separator...' summary sentence. Do not assume either fully-delimited or non-delimited encoding without SME confirmation (SEG132-SME-004).
